what_it_does: This paper tackles the problem of jitter (unwanted noise) in the clock signals that drive all digital chips. Most of the clock comes from two places: a crystal oscillator (a vibrating piece of quartz that keeps time) and a phase-locked loop (PLL)—a feedback circuit that cleans up the crystal's signal. Normally, engineers tune these separately. This work shows that treating them as a single system and optimizing them together reduces the total noise in the final clock signal. The key innovation is a 'self-aligned pulse-injection driver' that lets the crystal and the PLL talk more efficiently, achieving 4.6 GHz operation with very low noise (63.3 femtoseconds) while including the oscillator's own power consumption in the final quality score.
